# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 22 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Thanksgiving Hymns Column 22 where the three translators significantly diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 22:3 — "stubbornness of heart" — rendering of sherirut lev

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-stubbornness-of their heart" | Hyphenated construct preserving Hebrew bound form |
| LOGOS | "the stubbornness of their heart" | Standard scholarly rendering without hyphenation |
| PNEUMA | "with stubborn hearts" | Simplified adjectival form for readability |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "Stubbornness of their heart" is the recognized rendering of this key Qumran phrase. PNEUMA's adjectival simplification loses the noun-based Hebrew idiom.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 22:5 — "gathered together" vs. "conspired" vs. "plotted together"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "they have gathered-together against Your covenant" | Literal rendering of the Hebrew verb |
| LOGOS | "they conspired against Your covenant" | "Conspired" captures the hostile intent |
| PNEUMA | "they plotted together against Your covenant" | Dynamic equivalent emphasizing deliberate malice |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "Conspired" is concise and captures both the gathering and the hostile intent implicit in the Hebrew context.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 22:8 — "Belial" vs. "the Evil One" — sectarian demonological term

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "plans-of Belial" | Preserved as sectarian proper name |
| LOGOS | "schemes of Belial" | Preserved as proper name with stronger English noun |
| PNEUMA | "plots of the Evil One" | Functional equivalent for modern readers |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "Belial" is a proper name in Qumran theology (the chief adversary figure in the Community Rule and War Scroll) and must be preserved. "The Evil One" is too generic and could be confused with NT "ho poneros."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Sectarian proper names must be preserved.

---

## 22:8 — "double heart" vs. "divided heart" vs. "divided loyalty"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a double heart" | Literal lev va-lev |
| LOGOS | "a divided heart" | Standard English idiom for duplicity |
| PNEUMA | "divided loyalty" | Abstract noun replacing the body-part metaphor |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "Divided heart" preserves the body-part imagery of the Hebrew while being immediately comprehensible. PNEUMA's "divided loyalty" abandons the heart metaphor that is central to Hodayot anthropology.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 22:11 — "the dust" vs. "the dust-born" vs. "those made from dust"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-ear-of the-dust" | Hyper-literal; "dust" as metonymy for humanity |
| LOGOS | "the ear of the dust-born" | "Dust-born" clarifies the metonymy |
| PNEUMA | "the ears of those made from dust" | Full expansion of the metonymy |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "Dust-born" is an elegant compound that clarifies the metonymy without the wordiness of PNEUMA's expansion.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 22:18 — "sons of Adam" vs. "humankind"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-sons-of Adam" | Literal bene 'adam |
| LOGOS | "the sons of Adam" | Preserves Hebraic idiom |
| PNEUMA | "humankind" | Modern English equivalent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "Sons of Adam" is a significant theological expression in DSS texts, linking humanity to its created origin. "Humankind" loses this connection.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 22:30 — "consuming fire" word order and scope

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "into the-fire, consuming for eternity" | Separates fire from its consuming quality |
| LOGOS | "into the consuming fire for all eternity" | Unified phrase with temporal scope |
| PNEUMA | "into a fire that burns forever" | Dynamic relative clause |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "Consuming fire" is a unified biblical phrase (cf. Deut 4:24), and "for all eternity" naturally follows as the temporal modifier.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
